clarifyingQuestions: Does max wait start at first request arrival or every request arrival?
Should batches have token limits in addition to count limits?
In a production extension, should late arrivals join a due batch or the next batch? The base contract includes them.
followUps: Add a max token budget per batch.
Separate queues by model or priority class.
Make scheduler thread-safe for multiple request handlers.
followUpGuide: Token limits require storing token count per request and checking both count and token constraints.
Separate queues prevent one model or priority class from blocking another.
Thread safety needs one lock around queue mutation and flush decisions.
complexityAnalysis: - Immediate execution: run each request alone. Scheduling time: O(1) and no pending batch, but this gives up the opportunity to share an inference call.

- Batching deque: add is O(1) when it does not emit and O(k) when it returns k requests. A due or forced flush is O(k), or O(1) when nothing is emitted. Each arrival is appended and emitted once, so scheduling is amortized O(1) per request. Space: O(B), where B is max_batch_size, including an emitted batch.
- Priority batching follow-up: heap or multiple queues by deadline/priority. Time: O(log n) enqueue/dequeue. Space: O(n).
solutionGuide: Store `(arrival_ms, request_id)` in a deque. add checks capacity; flush_due checks only the oldest arrival. Never restart its timer when a later request arrives. Emission copies every pending ID in FIFO order and clears the deque, so the next batch gets a new oldest arrival. No autonomous timer or concurrency is assumed.
